---
title: "Table 3 — Darwin Core rank columns vs WoRMS AphiaID subtrees"
subtitle: "The same taxon group counted two ways"
---

```{r setup}
source("_common.R")
```

Store: `r store_label`

A user who filters `class = 'Actinopterygii'` gets nothing, because WoRMS files
Actinopterygii as a gigaclass and OBIS's `class` column carries Teleostei. The
AphiaID subtree is rank-agnostic. Each preset below is counted both ways on the
base resolution tier of `occ_h3`.

```{r table3}
rv <- calc_rank_vs_subtree(con)
rv |>
  mutate(across(c(records_rank, records_tree), ~ format(.x, big.mark = ",")),
         ratio = round(ratio, 3))
write.csv(rv, file.path(dir_fig, "tab3_rank_vs_subtree.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r fig-table3}
long <- bind_rows(
  transmute(rv, label, method = "DwC rank column", records = records_rank),
  transmute(rv, label, method = "AphiaID subtree", records = records_tree))
p <- ggplot(long, aes(x = reorder(label, -records), y = pmax(records, 0.5), fill = method)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = .8), width = .7) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "records (log)", fill = NULL,
       title = "Records found by rank-column filter vs AphiaID subtree",
       subtitle = "zero-height bars are groups the rank column cannot express",
       caption = store_label) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))
save_fig(p, "tab3_rank_vs_subtree", long, width = 9, height = 5)
p
```
